correctness.rationale: For every integer dimension at least three, the exact known parity-polytope inequalities cut a disjoint unit right simplex from each odd-weight cube corner. There are exactly half as many such corners as cube vertices, yielding volume \(1-2^{d-1}/d!\). Exact normalized monomial integration over a simplex computes the missing second moments, while coordinate permutation and even-complement symmetries force centroid at one-half and scalar covariance. This supplies a complete proof of the isotropic-constant formula, not numerical extrapolation. Exact strict rational comparisons at dimensions three through six, a formula proving increasing covariance from dimension five, and a dimension-seven rational barrier exclude every other dimension. Strict cube comparisons and the first-order factorial asymptotic follow from the same formula. The local exact-rational checker and independent finite convex-hull volume checks passed; no general claim relies on finite experiments.

value.rationale: The affine-invariant isotropic constant is a standard central invariant of high-dimensional convex geometry, and demihypercubes are a canonical infinite class of parity-code and type-D orbit polytopes. A complete exact all-dimensional formula, a proven nonmonotone dimension profile with unique minimum at five, a strict cube comparison and a sharp factorial perturbation law form a natural meaningful classification. It is not an arbitrary slice or a re-expression of a known table: the conclusion requires a new dissection-to-interior-covariance argument and rigorous all-dimension inequality.
